title: On the (Un)usefulness of Things
text:
A

        scarecrow,

        in the middle of a summer-scorched sea of wheat,

        watches over no one

        consciously.

        But it is not useless, for it takes care of absence.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the parenthetical title and the spare paradox of a scarecrow guarding absence.

title: Trilce: Poem XXVII - I Am Afraid of That Jet
text:
I am afraid of that jet,

good memory, strong lord, implacable

cruel sweetness. I am afraid.

This house gives me complete good, a complete

place for this not knowing where to be.


Let us not enter. I am afraid of this favor

of returning for minutes, over blown-up bridges.

I do not advance, sweet lord,

valiant memory, sad

singing skeleton.


What content this enchanted house has;

it gives me quicksilver deaths, and plugs

with lead my intakes

to the dry present.


The jet that knows nothing of how we are going

frightens me, gives me dread.

Valiant memory, I do not advance.

Blond and sad skeleton, whistle, whistle.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Vallejo's fractured Trilce logic: the jet, memory, house, and singing skeleton remain unstable.
